- When sentiment is high (≥0.85) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast shows strong downward bias, increase forecast by 2–5% to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), reduce subsequent forecast by 1–3% to correct for momentum overcorrection.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after trough), adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent history.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.3 in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from next forecast.
